change: Rewrote the arch-v2 SCReLU head a second time, from i32-lane arithmetic to an i16 multiply feeding a widening i16xi16->i32 multiply-accumulate (the pmaddwd/smlal shape). Added a dispatch so models quantized above QA=255 take an all-i64 path that is exact for any QA.

correctness.note: Signature unchanged from the post-S3 baseline, so the search tree is bit-identical. All 4 arch-v2 parity fixtures pass, including python_exported_gold_model_evaluates_identically. 56 cargo test targets green.
correctness.latent_bug_fixed: The previous kernel guarded its i32 accumulation with a debug_assert bounding QA to about 512. debug_assert is a no-op in release, so a model quantized with a larger QA would have overflowed i32 silently in production. The new screlu_dot_wide fallback is exact for any QA and is selected automatically.

measurement.method: criterion, PieBot/benches/nnue_v2_head_bench.rs, synthetic h1024 PIENNQ02 model. Random weights are valid here because these benches time kernels directly with no search tree, so the degenerate-eval caveat that applies to NPS measurements does not apply.

cost_split_h1024.note: The cache-realistic bench cycles through every legal move of a midgame position so feature rows are not L1-resident. It agrees with the ~488 ns/node eval cost derived independently from the box NPS numbers (v1 h64 2.139M vs v2 h1024 1.185M).

conclusion: Hand-written SIMD intrinsics are NOT the lever for arch-v2 speed, and this measurement supersedes the standing assumption that they were the top search arm. The head is only 38% of NNUE node cost and already sits near its instruction floor (about 8 ops per 8 lanes; 181 ns measured against a ~160 ns theoretical floor), which is why the portable i16-madd restructure captured only 1.10x and why explicit intrinsics have little left to take. The remaining 62% is the accumulator update, which is memory-latency-bound: w1 is 83.9 MB at h1024 (40960 features x 1024 x 2 bytes) and each quiet move pulls four scattered 2 KB rows, so roughly a third of that half is pure miss latency that no vectorization can remove. The fused accumulator update then took a further 7-14% off the other half by removing a redundant accumulator pass and overlapping the two row misses - again an access-pattern win, not a vectorization win, which reinforces the same conclusion.
next_levers_in_order: Deferred/lazy accumulator updates. alphabeta.rs:1237 calls apply_move eagerly for every searched move, but eval_current is only needed at a subset of nodes (children cut off by TT hits or immediate fail-high never need it). Stockfish defers with a dirty-piece accumulator stack. PAYOFF IS UNMEASURED and may be modest, because qsearch needs a stand-pat eval at essentially every node and qsearch dominates node counts - instrument the eval-per-apply ratio before building this.

Prefetch the feature rows at the top of apply_delta. There are only 2-4 rows per perspective and they are known before the loop starts, so issuing all the loads up front converts serial dependent misses into memory-level parallelism against the ~100 ns miss component.
Shrink the feature table. 83.9 MB is the root cause of the miss traffic; feature factorization or king bucketing would cut both the table and the miss rate.

fused_accumulator_update.change: apply_delta walked the accumulator once per feature row. The quiet-move case (exactly one feature out and one in per perspective) now walks it once, halving accumulator load/store traffic and issuing both w1 row reads in the same iteration so their cache misses overlap instead of serializing. Captures, promotions, castling and en passant keep the general path.
fused_accumulator_update.correctness: incremental_updates_match_full_recompute_over_random_games still passes (it exercises captures, promotions, castling and en passant, i.e. both paths), and matein3 still signs 20110404.

cumulative_vs_pre_optimization_baseline.note: Both changes together, measured against commit f082fe0 on the same machine and bench.
cumulative_vs_pre_optimization_baseline.estimated_box_nps_effect: If the ~56 ns/node saved on NEON carries to AVX2, the box's 843.8 ns/node drops to ~788 ns, i.e. 1.185M -> ~1.27M NPS (+6.7%). ESTIMATE ONLY: derived from a Mac bench applied to a box node-time figure. Must be confirmed with nps_bench.py on the box using a trained v2 net at a quiet moment.
